summary: Client reconnect via websocket handoff truncates inline/base64 attachments and produces partial embed blocks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their app reconnects (websocket upgrade) during an in-progress streaming response, inline attachments (base64-encoded image blobs and short file embeds) are truncated or delivered as partial blocks. The truncated embeds break downstream parsing in the customer app and cause retries.

Impact:
- NotesAI reports ~8% of streaming sessions that cross a connection handoff result in partial/broken attachments for a subset of responses (affects customers generating images/video thumbnails embedded as base64).
- Customer considers this P1 because their UI shows broken image tiles and triggers retry storms.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod us-east with edge-proxy (customer->corp-proxy->redwood-edge) flow.
- Client uses websocket fallback (upgrade) after long-poll SSE timeout.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming request that includes an inline image/base64 chunk in the middle of the stream.
2) Trigger a client network change (cellular->wifi) causing the socket to close and client to re-establish via websocket upgrade.
3) Observe in the app that the embedded image chunk is truncated and subsequent message delimiters are shifted, causing JSON parse failures.

Observed behavior / logs provided:
- Customer log snippet shows the streaming choice with midstream attachment marker, then a websocket reconnect, then the resumed stream contains an incomplete base64 payload and a closing delimiter is missing.
- Support obtained edge-proxy traces (trace IDs included below) that show the original connection tear, and then a new websocket handshake that is routed to a different worker.
- No 5xx from Redwood; the serving runtime returned success and an end-of-stream; the issue surfaces during reassembly at the edge/proxy boundary.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Avoid switching transport mid-response (prefer SSE or persistent WS without forcing rebind).
- Configure client to request attachments as separate fetches (non-stream) until fix applied.

Requested customer SLA follow-up:
- Customer asked for next steps and ETA for a fix.
comments: Support (2026-03-08): Initial triage - collected client capture, edge-proxy traces (kibana ID: kb-2026-03-08-831750), and customer timestamps. Asked for pcap of client socket if reproducible.

Customer (NotesAI) (2026-03-08): Provided two example session IDs where the truncated embed occurred and a short screen recording showing broken image tiles. Provided app logs and a minimized repro script.

SRE (2026-03-09): Observed connection handoff between edge instances (edge-12 -> edge-7) at time of reconnect. No server-side error; suspect boundary coalescing or chunk reassembly at edge-proxy layer. Increasing keepalive frequency reduced frequency but did not eliminate problem.

Eng (2026-03-09): Reproduced with internal harness that simulates websocket upgrade mid-stream with an attachment chunk. Confirmed truncated base64 on resumed path when proxy does TCP splice + frame coalescing. Filed PR to add explicit attachment boundary markers to streaming envelope and to tighten resume framing parsing (see PR link).

Support (2026-03-10): Shared mitigation steps with customer and coordinated accelerated validation on dedicated tenant. Customer validated that forcing client to wait for stream end or to re-request attachment prevented the issue.

Eng (2026-03-11): Deployed patch to edge-proxy (edge-runner v2.14.3) to preserve per-chunk boundaries during handoff and added an integration test for mid-stream websocket upgrades. Monitoring for 24h. Marking ticket Resolved after two customer validation sessions.
Customer (NotesAI) (2026-03-11): Confirmed fix in prod for their tenant; no truncated attachments observed in 48h window. Thanks noted.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge-proxy coalesces small writes during TCP splice when upgrading to websocket, causing boundary bytes (attachment terminator) to be lost or merged with next frame.
Hypothesis 2: Resume logic expects stream-level offsets (SSE offsets) but websocket tunnel applies differing framing and the resume envelope mapper dropped a delimiter during conversion.

Finding: Repro harness (attached to repo) shows that when a base64 chunk is split exactly at TCP segment boundary and proxy performs a splice + buffer coalescing, the parsed resume frame omits the final '::BOUNDARY' marker used by SDKs to detect end-of-attachment. The serving runtime had delivered payload intact; corruption happened at edge-proxy handoff.

Action taken: Implemented conservative change in edge-runner to never coalesce frames containing 'attachment-marker' bytes and to preserve exact chunk boundaries across handoff. Added unit tests and end-to-end test that simulates client rebind.

customer session: notesai-session-20260308-5543 (client logs and base64 snippet attached)

resolution: Deployed edge-runner v2.14.3 which preserves chunk boundaries during websocket handoffs and added parsing hardening for attachment terminators. Customer validated fix on their dedicated tenant; follow-ups: update SDK docs to recommend explicit attachment delimiter handling and add a runbook entry for 'mid-stream transport change' under the support playbook. Patch PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-runner/pull/4123.
